newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Major speaks with Yeltsin, plans to visit Russia.
newsitem.headline: Major speaks with Yeltsin, plans to visit Russia.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin spoke to British Prime Minister John Major by telephone on Monday, the Russian leader's first day back in the Kremlin since his heart bypass operation seven weeks ago.
The two leaders agreed that Major would visit Russia in the new year but no date was fixed, the presidential press service said in a statement.
Major congratulated Yeltsin on his return to work after his recovery from heart surgery and the Russian leader expressed satisfaction with the current state of Anglo-Russian relations, it said.

Yeltsin said Russia was ready "for deeper cooperation in the economic, commercial and other spheres" and also urged Britain to bear in mind Moscow's concern about NATO's eastward expansion in its deliberations with other members of the Western alliance.
Russia is strongly opposed to NATO's plans to take in former communist countries in central and eastern Europe.

Among other world leaders, Yeltsin has also spoken with U.S. President Bill Clinton, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and French President Jacques Chirac since undergoing heart surgery on November 5. He plans to meet all three of them next year.
